auditor_persona: Senior staff backend engineer specialized in observability/SLO instrumentation, non-blocking telemetry, Laravel admin surfaces, and adversarial review of write paths exposed by authenticated POST endpoints. Adversarial mindset: hunt for unbounded cardinality, missing branch isolation, telemetry that can break business flows under DB pressure, percentile math errors, missing throttling, and frontend buffers that can leak listeners or grow unbounded.

audit_axes: G1 — Non-blocking guarantee end-to-end: confirm that a DB failure during recordEventDispatched() inside DispatchDomainEventsJob::handle() success branch does NOT (a) leave a stale last_error in domain_events, (b) cause the job to throw and re-attempt, (c) silently drop the dispatched_at finalisation. Walk the failure path: recorder.insertMetric throws → caught in recorder → Log::warning → returns void → handle()'s defensive try/catch is no-op → forceFill(['last_error' => null])->save() runs normally. Confirm correctness.

G2 — Branch isolation: verify the GET /sync-overview controller filters by branch_id ONLY when supplied as a query param (no implicit user.branch_id default). Could a non-admin authenticated user query branch_id != their_branch and see other branches' metrics? Audit the auth/authorization gap. The route lives inside Route::prefix('admin') with auth:sanctum but no explicit role check. Flag if cross-branch leakage is possible (this is the F-21 frozen zone risk equivalent for observability).

G3 — Throttling vs. cardinality: GET /sync-overview has only the inherited throttle:admin-mutation; POST /client-metrics adds throttle:60,1. With maxBatch=200 client-side, max ingest = 200 * 60 = 12 000 rows/min/IP. Confirm this is the intended ceiling and that the bigInteger column + indexes can sustain it. Also: is the limit:50000 in the SELECT a real cap or a footgun (silently truncates p99 on a busy branch)?

G4 — Whitelist enforcement: the recorder's recordClientMetric uses ALLOWED_CLIENT_METRICS but the FormRequest also enforces Rule::in(...). Confirm the two whitelists are sourced from the SAME constant (no drift risk). Audit recordEventDispatched, recordWebSocketAuthFailure, recordKdsSyncFallback: these bypass the whitelist by design (server-side only) — confirm intent and that no unauthenticated route exposes them.

G5 — Percentile math (nearest-rank): the controller computes percentile via `index = ceil(p/100 * N) - 1` clamped to [0, N-1]. Verify edge cases: N=1 (any percentile returns the only value), N=2 with p=50 (returns index 0 = lower of the two; nearest-rank convention; document if intentional). For N=100 the test asserts p50=50, p95=95, p99=99 — confirm these match the formula.

G6 — Correlation ID propagation: the recorder's resolveCorrelationId falls back to request()->header('X-Correlation-ID') when no explicit arg. In a queue worker context (DispatchDomainEventsJob::handle), there is NO request — confirm the recorder's `function_exists('request') && request()` guard returns null gracefully (does it? request() is always defined in Laravel; it returns null when no request is bound, but a try/catch is in place). Walk through the queue path explicitly.

G7 — Frontend buffer leak / listener leak: MetricsBatcher.destroy() pops every unsubscriber. Verify the on() contract from NEW-02 (returns a function) is honoured by both wsService AND any future kdsSyncService. The `subscribe()` helper has a fallback for services that expose `off()` instead of returning an unsubscribe — confirm this is correct. Also: the lastKdsReasonByTransition Map grows unbounded in long sessions (one entry per (from,to) pair × reasons). Quantify: is the cardinality bounded (yes, KDS state machine has ~5 states × 4 reasons = ~20 entries max)?

G8 — Buffer FIFO drop semantics: when buffer.length >= cappedMaxBatch, pushMetric does buffer.shift() (drops OLDEST). Confirm this is the intended drop policy (newest wins) and that it matches the backend retention strategy. Alternative: drop newest (preserves history). Document the trade-off.

G9 — Correlation ID source order on the frontend: readCorrelationId() prefers globalThis.window.__correlationId, then localStorage. Verify this order matches the global pattern used by HasCorrelationId trait + CorrelationIdMiddleware, and that the middleware writes to one of these slots (or document the gap and how the global is hydrated).

G10 — POST endpoint authorization model: the StoreClientMetricsRequest.authorize() returns `$this->user() !== null` — any authenticated admin can submit metrics on behalf of their branch. Confirm this is the intended trust boundary and that branch_id is server-derived (it is — from $request->user()->branch_id) and NOT taken from the payload. Flag if the payload could ever inject a branch_id.
